brief: The canvas depicts a massive geological cross-section, showing stacked layers of colorful sedimentary and metamorphic rock. The scene is dominated by the visible action of tectonic forces, which apply slow, constant pressure and stress to the rock mass. Over the course of the sketch, these forces cause visible slippage along fault lines, generating fault gouge and movement. This continuous process results in the slow, gradual uplift of the rock layers, forming mountainous peaks and shifting the entire continental crust across the observable field of view.

statement: This sketch portrays the slow, continuous process of geological uplift through tectonic forces. It depicts stacked sedimentary and metamorphic rock layers under constant pressure, with visible fault lines where stress accumulates and releases. As time progresses, the landscape slowly shifts and rises, creating mountain peaks and shifting crustal features across the field of view. The animation shows how continuous geological processes shape the Earth's surface over immense timescales, with visual cues like slippage along fault lines and fault gouge particles illustrating the dynamic nature of these forces.
